c.v: Kai jogged 2 km 400 m in the morning and 1 km 800 m in the evening. How far did he jog altogether? Choose the answer in metres.
Change each distance to metres: 2 km 400 m = 2400 m and 1 km 800 m = 1800 m.
3200 is what you get if the 1 km is left out of 1 km 800 m. 4100 comes from a mistake in regrouping the hundreds.
Zul wants to run 5 km. He has already run 4 rounds of a path that is 750 m long. How many more metres must he run? Choose the answer in metres.
4 rounds of the path = 4 × 750 m = 3000 m.
3000 m is the distance Zul has already run. 4250 m is what you get if only 1 round is taken away.
A jug has 2 ℓ of water. Rani pours 300 ml of water into each of 5 cups. How much water is left in the jug? Choose the answer in millilitres.
5 cups × 300 ml = 1500 ml of water poured out.
1500 ml is the amount poured out, not the amount left. 1700 ml comes from taking away only 1 cup.
Mrs Tay uses a 500 ml mug to fill an empty pot with water. The pot holds 3 ℓ. How many mugs of water does she need to fill the pot?
Every 2 mugs make 1 ℓ (500 ml + 500 ml = 1000 ml), so 3 ℓ needs 3 × 2 = 6 mugs.
3 is the number of litres, not the number of mugs.
Which of the following statements is correct?
5 ℓ 7 ml = 5070 ml
3 m 6 cm = 360 cm
Check each one by changing to the smaller unit.
2 kg 30 g = 2000 g + 30 g = 2030 g. This is correct.
5 ℓ 7 ml = 5007 ml, not 5070 ml.
3 m 6 cm = 306 cm, not 360 cm.
A watermelon has a mass of 2 kg 300 g. A pineapple is 850 g lighter than the watermelon. What is the mass of the pineapple? Choose the answer in grams.
3150 g is what you get if 850 g is added instead of taken away.
Mrs Yeo needs 1 ℓ 250 ml of milk to make one batch of pudding. She makes 3 batches. She has 5 ℓ of milk at first.
How much milk does she have left? Give your answer in ℓ and ml.
Milk for 3 batches: 3 × 1 ℓ 250 ml = 3 ℓ 750 ml (or 3 × 1250 ml = 3750 ml).
She has 1 ℓ 250 ml of milk left.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the milk used for 3 batches (3750 ml or 3 ℓ 750 ml)
Subtracts the milk used from 5 ℓ (5000 ml)
Writes the answer as 1 ℓ 250 ml

c.v: Wei Jie cycled from his home to the park, a distance of 1 km 850 m. He then cycled 2 km 300 m to the library. Finally he cycled 3 km 400 m from the library back home.
How far did he cycle altogether? Give your answer in km and m.
Change the distances to metres: 1 km 850 m = 1850 m, 2 km 300 m = 2300 m, 3 km 400 m = 3400 m.
Wei Jie cycled 7 km 550 m altogether.

partialMarks.criterion: Changes the three distances to metres (or adds km and m separately)
Adds correctly to get 7550 m
Writes the answer as 7 km 550 m

familyTitle: Bus to Stop C and back

c.v: A bus travels from Stop A to Stop B, a distance of 2 km. It then travels 750 m to Stop C. The bus then goes back to Stop A along the same road.
How far does the bus travel altogether? Give your answer in km and m.
Stop A to Stop C = 2 km + 750 m = 2 km 750 m = 2750 m.
The bus goes there and back, so the total distance is 2 × 2750 m = 5500 m.
The bus travels 5 km 500 m altogether.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the distance from Stop A to Stop C (2 km 750 m or 2750 m)
Doubles the distance for the return trip (5500 m)
Writes the answer as 5 km 500 m

c.v: Ali drank 250 ml of milk every day for 6 days. Farid drank 350 ml of milk every day for 4 days.
How many more millilitres of milk did Ali drink than Farid?
Farid: 4 × 350 ml = 1400 ml.
Ali drank 100 ml more than Farid.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the amount Ali drank (1500 ml)
Finds the amount Farid drank (1400 ml)
Subtracts to get 100 ml

c.v: A shop had 10 kg of rice. It sold 3 bags of rice, each with a mass of 2 kg 500 g. Later it sold another 1 kg 750 g of rice.
How much rice was left? Give your answer in kg and g.
Total sold: 7500 g + 1750 g = 9250 g.
750 g of rice was left.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the mass of the 3 bags (7500 g or 7 kg 500 g)
Adds the other 1 kg 750 g to get 9250 g sold
Subtracts from 10 kg to get 750 g

c.v: Mrs Rao had a rope 5 m long. She cut 3 pieces, each 85 cm long, for a skipping game.
How many centimetres of rope were left?
3 pieces: 3 × 85 cm = 255 cm.
245 cm of rope was left.

partialMarks.criterion: Changes 5 m to 500 cm
Finds the length of the 3 pieces (255 cm)
Subtracts to get 245 cm

c.v: Amir jogs 1 km 200 m every morning from Monday to Friday. On Saturday he jogs 2 km 50 m.
How far does he jog from Monday to Saturday? Give your answer in km and m.
Monday to Friday: 5 × 1 km 200 m = 5 × 1200 m = 6000 m.
Saturday: 2 km 50 m = 2050 m.
Amir jogs 8 km 50 m altogether.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the distance for 5 days (6000 m or 6 km)
Adds the distance on Saturday to get 8050 m
Writes the answer as 8 km 50 m

c.v: Lena swims one length of a pool in 45 s. She swims 4 lengths without stopping. How many minutes does she take?
4 lengths take 4 × 45 s = 180 s.
60 s = 1 min, so 180 s = 3 min.
180 is the time in seconds, but the question asks for minutes.
Ah Kow took 2 min 15 s to solve puzzle A and 95 s to solve puzzle B. How many seconds longer did he take to solve puzzle A?
Change 2 min 15 s to seconds: 2 × 60 s + 15 s = 135 s.
120 comes from wrongly writing 2 min 15 s as 215 s. 230 comes from adding instead of subtracting.
A film ended at 5.10 p.m. It lasted 1 h 45 min. At what time did the film start?
Go back 1 h from 5.10 p.m. to get 4.10 p.m.
Go back another 45 min: 4.10 p.m. – 45 min = 3.25 p.m.
6.55 p.m. is what you get by adding instead of going back. 4.25 p.m. is what you get if only 45 min is taken away.
A tuition class started at 4.50 p.m. and ended at 6.20 p.m. There was a 15-minute break during the class. For how many minutes did the pupils have lessons?
From 4.50 p.m. to 6.20 p.m.: 10 min + 1 h + 20 min = 90 min.
Take away the break: 90 min – 15 min = 75 min.
90 min is the length of the whole class. 105 min comes from adding the break. 170 comes from subtracting 450 from 620 without changing hours to minutes.
Kelly's train left at 2.45 p.m. and reached the station at 1735 h. How many minutes did the journey take?
Change 2.45 p.m. to the 24-hour clock: 1445 h.
From 1445 h to 1735 h: 15 min to 1500 h, then 2 h 35 min = 2 h 50 min.
2 h 50 min = 120 min + 50 min = 170 min.
290 comes from subtracting 1445 from 1735 as ordinary numbers.
Which of the following is the earliest time?
Change every time to the same clock. Use the 24-hour clock.
1245 h is the smallest, so it is the earliest time (12.45 p.m.).
Team A's three runners took 34 s, 41 s and 1 min 5 s to run their parts of a relay race. Team B took 2 min 35 s altogether.
How many seconds faster was Team A than Team B?
Team B: 2 min 35 s = 120 s + 35 s = 155 s.
Team A was 15 seconds faster.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds Team A's total time in seconds (140 s)
Changes Team B's time to seconds (155 s)
Subtracts to get 15 s

c.v: Uncle Lim takes 45 s to fry one plate of noodles. He fries 7 plates one after another. Then he takes 1 min 45 s to wash the wok.
How much time does he spend altogether? Give your answer in seconds.
7 plates: 7 × 45 s = 315 s.
He spends 420 seconds altogether.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the time to fry 7 plates (315 s)
Changes 1 min 45 s to 105 s
Adds to get 420 s

c.v: Mrs Chua's class left school at 8.45 a.m. to go to a museum. The bus ride took 50 minutes. The class then spent 2 h 30 min at the museum.
At what time did the class leave the museum? Use a.m. or p.m. in your answer.
8.45 a.m. + 50 min = 9.35 a.m. (the class reached the museum).
The class left the museum at 12.05 p.m.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the arrival time at the museum (9.35 a.m.)
Adds 2 h 30 min correctly to get 12.05
Writes p.m. for the time after noon

c.v: Ms Ng's tuition class started at 3.50 p.m. There were two lessons of 55 minutes each, with a 10-minute break between them.
At what time did the class end? Use a.m. or p.m. in your answer.
First lesson: 3.50 p.m. + 55 min = 4.45 p.m.
Break: 4.45 p.m. + 10 min = 4.55 p.m.
Second lesson: 4.55 p.m. + 55 min = 5.50 p.m.
The class ended at 5.50 p.m.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the end of the first lesson (4.45 p.m.)
Adds the 10-minute break (4.55 p.m.)
Adds the second lesson to get 5.50 p.m.

c.v: Mira's MRT ride started at 7.40 a.m. and ended at 8.25 a.m. Her father's journey by bus took 25 minutes longer than Mira's ride. He left home at 7.20 a.m.
At what time did her father arrive? Use a.m. or p.m. in your answer.
Mira's ride: 7.40 a.m. to 8.25 a.m. = 20 min + 25 min = 45 min.
Her father's journey: 45 min + 25 min = 70 min = 1 h 10 min.
Her father arrived at 8.30 a.m.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the length of Mira's ride (45 min)
Finds the length of her father's journey (70 min or 1 h 10 min)
Adds to 7.20 a.m. to get 8.30 a.m.

c.v: Farah's flight took off at 2015 h and lasted 3 h 50 min. Ignore any difference in time zones.
At what time did the flight land? Write your answer using the 24-hour clock.
2315 h + 45 min = 0000 h (midnight), so there are 5 more minutes to add for the 50 min.
The flight landed at 0005 h the next day.

partialMarks.criterion: Adds 3 h to get 2315 h
Adds 50 min correctly, going past midnight
Writes the time as 0005 h in the 24-hour clock

c.v: A supermarket opens at 0830 h and closes at 2130 h from Monday to Friday. On Saturday it opens at 0730 h and closes at 2200 h.
How many more minutes is the supermarket open on Saturday than on a weekday?
Weekday: 0830 h to 2130 h = 13 h = 780 min.
Saturday: 0730 h to 2200 h = 14 h 30 min = 840 min + 30 min = 870 min.
870 min – 780 min = 90 min.
It is open 90 minutes (1 h 30 min) longer on Saturday.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the weekday opening time (13 h or 780 min)
Finds the Saturday opening time (14 h 30 min or 870 min)
Subtracts to get 90 min

c.v: A rectangular wall is 8 m long and 5 m high. Mrs Lee covers the whole wall with square tiles. Each tile covers an area of 1 m². How many tiles does she need?
The number of tiles is the area of the wall.
Area = length × height = 8 × 5 = 40 m².
So Mrs Lee needs 40 tiles.
13 comes from adding 8 + 5. 26 is the perimeter of the wall.
A rectangle is 14 cm long. Its width is 6 cm shorter than its length. What is the perimeter of the rectangle? Choose the answer in centimetres.
Width = 14 cm – 6 cm = 8 cm.
22 cm is only half of the perimeter. 40 cm comes from using 6 cm as the width.

familyTitle: Area from the perimeter of a square

c.v: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area? Choose the answer in cm².
A square has 4 equal sides, so one side = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm.
Area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².
9 is the length of one side. 18 is half of the perimeter.
Each side of a small square is 2 cm. What is the perimeter of the figure? Choose the answer in centimetres.
Count the sides going round the figure in squares: 4 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 4 = 16 squares.
Each side of a square is 2 cm, so the perimeter = 16 × 2 = 32 cm.
16 is the number of squares along the edge, not the length in cm. 48 is the area, not the perimeter.

familyTitle: Squares needed to fill a rectangle

c.v: Each square is 1 square unit. The shaded part is inside a rectangle drawn in dark lines. How many more squares must be shaded to fill the whole rectangle?
The rectangle is 5 squares long and 3 squares wide, so it has 5 × 3 = 15 squares.
9 squares are already shaded.
15 – 9 = 6, so 6 more squares must be shaded.
15 is the size of the whole rectangle. 9 is the number already shaded.
Rectangle A is 8 cm long and 2 cm wide. Square B has sides of 4 cm. Which statement is correct?
Rectangle A has the greater area.
Both shapes have the same perimeter.
Both shapes have the same area but different perimeters.
Square B has the greater perimeter.
Area of A = 8 × 2 = 16 cm². Area of B = 4 × 4 = 16 cm². The areas are the same.
Perimeter of A = 2 × (8 + 2) = 20 cm. Perimeter of B = 4 × 4 = 16 cm. The perimeters are different, and A has the greater perimeter.
Card A is a rectangle 15 cm long and 6 cm wide. Card B is a square with a perimeter of 40 cm.
What is the difference between the areas of the two cards? Give your answer in cm².
Area of Card A = 15 × 6 = 90 cm².
Side of Card B = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 cm.
Area of Card B = 10 × 10 = 100 cm².
100 cm² – 90 cm² = 10 cm².

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the area of Card A (90 cm²)
Finds the side (10 cm) and area (100 cm²) of Card B
Subtracts to get 10 cm²

c.v: Ali jogs 3 rounds around a rectangular field that is 45 m long and 25 m wide. He then walks 180 m to the bus stop.
How far does Ali jog and walk altogether? Give your answer in metres.
Perimeter of the field = 2 × (45 + 25) = 2 × 70 = 140 m.
3 rounds: 3 × 140 m = 420 m.
Ali jogs and walks 600 m altogether.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the perimeter of the field (140 m)
Multiplies by 3 for 3 rounds (420 m)
Adds the 180 m to get 600 m

c.v: A piece of wire is bent to make a square with sides of 12 cm. The wire is then straightened and bent to make a rectangle that is 16 cm long.
What is the width of the rectangle? Give your answer in centimetres.
Length of the wire = perimeter of the square = 4 × 12 = 48 cm.
The rectangle has the same perimeter, so length + width = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 cm.
Width = 24 cm – 16 cm = 8 cm.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the length of the wire (48 cm)
Finds length + width = 24 cm
Subtracts the length to get a width of 8 cm

c.v: The picture shows the plan of a T-shaped garden. Each side of a small square is 2 m. Mr Wong puts a fence round the whole edge of the garden.
How long is the fence? Give your answer in metres.
Count the length of each side going round the garden in squares: 6, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2 and 2.
Each side of a square is 2 m, so the fence is 20 × 2 = 40 m long.

partialMarks.criterion: Counts all 8 sides correctly (6, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2 squares)
Adds to get 20 squares
Multiplies by 2 m to get 40 m

c.v: Each side of a small square is 3 cm. Ling puts a ribbon round the edge of the figure. She needs another 10 cm of ribbon for a knot.
What is the total length of ribbon she needs? Give your answer in centimetres.
Count the sides round the figure in squares: 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3 and 3.
12 × 3 cm = 36 cm goes round the edge.
36 cm + 10 cm = 46 cm.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the distance round the figure in squares (12)
Changes to centimetres (36 cm)
Adds the 10 cm for the knot to get 46 cm

c.v: A rectangle has an area of 72 cm². Its length is 9 cm.
What is the perimeter of the rectangle? Give your answer in centimetres.
Width = area ÷ length = 72 ÷ 9 = 8 cm.
Length + width = 9 + 8 = 17 cm.
Perimeter = 2 × 17 = 34 cm.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the width (8 cm)
Finds length + width (17 cm)
Doubles to get the perimeter 34 cm

c.v: The shaded part shows the plan of a floor. Each square has an area of 4 m². Mr Tan covers the floor with carpet that costs $3 for every square metre.
How much does the carpet cost?
Count the shaded squares: 3 + 5 + 3 = 11 squares.
Area of the floor = 11 × 4 m² = 44 m².

partialMarks.criterion: Counts the 11 shaded squares
Finds the area of the floor (44 m²)
Multiplies by $3 to get $132

c.v: Mr Ho cuts a square piece of cloth into 2 equal rectangles. How many right angles are there in the 2 rectangles altogether?
Each rectangle has 4 corners and every corner is a right angle.
2 rectangles have 2 × 4 = 8 right angles.
4 is the number of right angles in the square before it was cut.

familyTitle: Compare three angles with a right angle

c.v: Look at angles X, Y and Z. Which statement is correct?
X and Z are smaller than a right angle.
Only angle Z is greater than a right angle.
Angle Y is smaller than a right angle.
Angles X and Y are both right angles.
Compare each angle with the corner of a piece of paper (a right angle).
X is smaller than a right angle. Y is a right angle. Z is greater than a right angle.
So only angle Z is greater than a right angle.
Jia opens her laptop screen slowly from closed. The screen and the keyboard make an angle. Which shows how the angle changes as the screen opens?
It goes from greater than a right angle, to a right angle, to smaller than a right angle.
It goes from a right angle, to smaller than a right angle, to greater than a right angle.
It goes from smaller than a right angle, to greater than a right angle, to a right angle.
It goes from smaller than a right angle, to a right angle, to greater than a right angle.
When the screen is closed there is almost no gap, so the angle is very small.
As it opens, the angle gets bigger: first smaller than a right angle, then a right angle, then greater than a right angle.
How many of angles Q, R and S are greater than angle P?
An angle is greater when its arms open wider. The length of the arms does not matter.
Q opens wider than P. R opens less than P. S opens wider than P.
So 2 angles (Q and S) are greater than angle P.
Rui draws angles P, Q and R. She says one is a right angle, one is smaller than a right angle and one is greater than a right angle. Which angle is the right angle?
Angle P
Angle Q
Angle R
None of the angles
Compare each angle with the corner of a piece of paper.
P is wider than the corner, so it is greater than a right angle. R is narrower, so it is smaller than a right angle. Q fits the corner exactly, so Q is the right angle.

familyTitle: Between a right angle and angle S

c.v: Which angle is greater than a right angle but smaller than angle S?
Angle S
Angle P
Angle R
Angle Q
Angles P and Q are smaller than a right angle, so they cannot be the answer.
Angle S is greater than a right angle, but it is not smaller than itself.
Angle R is greater than a right angle and smaller than angle S, so R is the answer.
Mr Ong has 5 square tiles. He cuts 2 of the square tiles, each into 2 equal rectangles.
How many right angles are there on all his tiles now?
The 3 tiles he did not cut are still squares: 3 × 4 = 12 right angles.
The 2 cut tiles make 2 × 2 = 4 rectangles: 4 × 4 = 16 right angles.
12 + 16 = 28 right angles.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the right angles on the 3 uncut squares (12)
Finds the right angles on the 4 rectangles (16)
Adds to get 28

c.v: Each set square has 1 right angle and 2 angles that are smaller than a right angle. Mrs Chan has 6 set squares.
How many more angles smaller than a right angle than right angles are there in all 6 set squares?
Right angles: 6 × 1 = 6.
Angles smaller than a right angle: 6 × 2 = 12.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the number of right angles (6)
Finds the number of angles smaller than a right angle (12)
Subtracts to get 6

c.v: A rectangle has 4 angles. A triangle has 3 angles. Ben draws 5 rectangles. Amy draws 4 triangles.
How many more angles are in Ben's drawing than in Amy's drawing?
Ben: 5 × 4 = 20 angles.
Amy: 4 × 3 = 12 angles.
20 – 12 = 8 more angles.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the number of angles in Ben's rectangles (20)
Finds the number of angles in Amy's triangles (12)
Subtracts to get 8

c.v: Look at lines P, Q, R and S. Which statement is correct?
Line R is parallel to line S.
Line P is perpendicular to line Q.
Line R is perpendicular to line P.
Line S is perpendicular to line Q.
Lines P and Q are parallel to each other (they never meet), so P is not perpendicular to Q.
Line R stands straight up and meets line P at a square corner, so R is perpendicular to P.
Line S leans and is not parallel to R. It does not meet Q at a square corner either.
The figure is made of 5 straight lines. How many pairs of perpendicular lines are there?
Each of the 3 lines R, S and T is perpendicular to both line P and line Q.
Number of pairs = 3 × 2 = 6.
5 comes from adding 3 + 2. 12 comes from counting every pair twice.
Line P is parallel to line Q. Line R is perpendicular to line P. All three lines are drawn on the same flat sheet of paper. Which statement is correct?
Line R is parallel to line Q.
Line R meets line Q, but not at a right angle.
Line R is perpendicular to line Q.
We cannot tell how line R and line Q are related.
Lines P and Q go in the same direction. A line that makes a square corner with P also makes a square corner with Q.
So line R is perpendicular to line Q.

familyTitle: Which point makes a parallel line

c.v: Ben joins point X to one of the points P, Q, R or S. Which point should he join to X to draw a line that is parallel to line KL?
Point R
Point Q
Point S
Point P
From K to L the line goes 3 squares across and 2 squares up.
A parallel line goes the same way: from X, go 3 squares across and 2 squares up. This reaches point P.
Point Q is 2 across and 3 up, which is a different slope.
Look at lines P, Q, R and S. Which statement is correct?
Line P is parallel to line R, and both are perpendicular to line Q.
Line P is perpendicular to line R.
Line Q is parallel to line R.
Line Q is perpendicular to line S.
Lines P and R both run across, so they are parallel to each other.
Line Q runs up and down and meets P and R at square corners, so Q is perpendicular to both.
Lines Q and S both run up and down, so they are parallel, not perpendicular.

familyTitle: Steps to draw a parallel line

c.v: Ben wants to draw a line through point X that is parallel to line AB. He places one edge of a set square along line AB and holds a ruler firmly against another edge of the set square. He then slides the set square along the ruler until the first edge touches point X. What should Ben do next?
Draw a line along the ruler.
Draw a line along the edge at a right angle to line AB.
Draw a line from X to any point on line AB.
Draw a line along the edge of the set square that now touches X.
Sliding the set square along the ruler keeps the edge pointing the same way as when it was on line AB.
So a line drawn along that edge, through X, is parallel to line AB.
The figure shows a window frame made of 5 straight lines. How many more pairs of perpendicular lines than pairs of parallel lines are there?
Perpendicular pairs: each of P and Q is perpendicular to R, S and T. That is 2 × 3 = 6 pairs.
Parallel pairs: P and Q make 1 pair. R, S and T make 3 pairs (R and S, R and T, S and T). That is 1 + 3 = 4 pairs.
6 – 4 = 2 more pairs.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the number of perpendicular pairs (6)
Finds the number of parallel pairs (4)
Subtracts to get 2

c.v: Each ladder has 2 long sides that are parallel to each other and 4 rungs. Every rung is perpendicular to both long sides. In each of 3 ladders, 1 rung has broken off.
How many pairs of perpendicular lines are there in the 3 ladders now?
Each ladder now has 4 – 1 = 3 rungs.
Each rung is perpendicular to both sides, so each ladder has 3 × 2 = 6 pairs of perpendicular lines.
3 ladders: 3 × 6 = 18 pairs.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the number of rungs left on each ladder (3)
Finds the pairs on one ladder (6)
Multiplies by 3 to get 18

familyTitle: Tuesday and Thursday against Monday and Wednesday

stem.title: Books borrowed from the school library

c.v: How many more books were borrowed on Tuesday and Thursday together than on Monday and Wednesday together?
Tuesday and Thursday: 45 + 40 = 85 books.
Monday and Wednesday: 30 + 25 = 55 books.
85 is the total for Tuesday and Thursday only. 55 is the total for Monday and Wednesday only.

familyTitle: Most popular and least popular foods

stem.title: Favourite hawker food of Primary 3 pupils

c.v: Each pupil chose one food. How many fewer pupils chose the two least popular foods than the two most popular foods?
The two most popular foods are chicken rice (18) and roti prata (16): 18 + 16 = 34 pupils.
The two least popular foods are mee goreng (10) and laksa (12): 10 + 12 = 22 pupils.
34 – 22 = 12 fewer pupils.

familyTitle: Fair tickets with a scale of 100

stem.title: Tickets sold at the school fair

c.v: A bar that ends between two gridlines ends exactly halfway between them. How many more tickets were sold on Thursday and Friday together than on Monday and Wednesday together?
Each gridline goes up by 100 tickets, so a bar halfway between two gridlines shows 50 more than the lower gridline.
Thursday and Friday: 350 + 500 = 850 tickets. Monday and Wednesday: 250 + 150 = 400 tickets.

This week, Chen wants to read as many minutes as Bala read last week. He can add 5 more minutes to his reading each day. In how many days will Chen have added enough minutes to catch up with Bala's total?
Bala: 40 minutes. Chen: 15 minutes. Chen needs 40 – 15 = 25 more minutes.
8 comes from dividing Bala's total by 5. 3 comes from dividing Chen's total by 5.

familyTitle: A fifth seller not on the graph

stem.title: Tickets sold for the school concert

c.v: Eva also sold tickets. She sold as many tickets as Ann and Dan together. How many tickets did the 5 pupils sell altogether?
The 4 pupils on the graph sold 14 + 8 + 12 + 6 = 40 tickets.
Eva sold 14 + 6 = 20 tickets.
40 + 20 = 60 tickets.
40 is the total without Eva.

familyTitle: Which reading of the graph is true

stem.title: Cups of drinks sold at a kopitiam

c.v: A bar that ends between two gridlines ends exactly halfway between them. Which statement about the graph is correct?
Kopi sold 40 cups.
Milo sold half as many cups as lemon tea.
Lemon tea sold 10 more cups than kopi.
Teh and Milo together sold more cups than lemon tea.
Each gridline goes up by 10 cups. Kopi is halfway between 40 and 50, so it sold 45 cups. Lemon tea sold 55 cups.
55 – 45 = 10, so lemon tea sold 10 more cups than kopi.
Milo (20) is not half of 55. Teh and Milo together sold 30 + 20 = 50 cups, which is fewer than 55.
Each set of kaya toast costs $3. How much money was collected from the sets sold on Tuesday and Thursday?
Tuesday: 35 sets. Thursday: 40 sets.
$225 was collected on Tuesday and Thursday.

partialMarks.criterion: Reads the bars correctly (35 and 40)
Adds to get 75 sets
Multiplies by $3 to get $225

stem.title: Number of pupils in each club

c.v: The principal wants each club to have 20 pupils. How many more pupils are needed altogether for the clubs that have fewer than 20 pupils?
The clubs with fewer than 20 pupils are Chess (12), Art (18) and Robotics (16).
More pupils needed: Chess 20 – 12 = 8, Art 20 – 18 = 2, Robotics 20 – 16 = 4.
8 + 2 + 4 = 14 pupils.

partialMarks.criterion: Picks out the 3 clubs with fewer than 20 pupils
Finds how many more each club needs (8, 2 and 4)
Adds to get 14

c.v: A bar that ends between two gridlines ends exactly halfway between them. How many more visitors came on Saturday and Sunday than on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday altogether?
Each gridline goes up by 100 visitors.
Saturday and Sunday: 450 + 350 = 800 visitors.
Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday: 150 + 250 + 200 = 600 visitors.
800 – 600 = 200 more visitors.

partialMarks.criterion: Reads the weekend bars using the scale (450 and 350)
Finds the weekday total (600)
Subtracts to get 200

c.v: The 3 pupils who exercised the longest want to exercise for 3 hours altogether. How many more minutes must they exercise?
The 3 longest times are Carl (45 min), Emy (40 min) and Ali (35 min).
3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 min.
180 min – 120 min = 60 min.

partialMarks.criterion: Picks the 3 longest times and adds them (120 min)
Changes 3 hours to 180 min
Subtracts to get 60 min

stem.title: Places chosen for the class trip

c.v: The pupils who chose the Zoo or the Museum will travel in vans. Each van carries 8 pupils. How many vans are needed?
Zoo: 24 pupils. Museum: 8 pupils.
24 + 8 = 32 pupils.

partialMarks.criterion: Reads the bars correctly (24 and 8)
Adds to get 32 pupils
Divides by 8 to get 4 vans

c.v: The two graphs use different scales. How many more books did Class 3B read than Class 3A altogether?
Look at the scale of each graph. Graph A goes up by 2 and graph B goes up by 5.
Class 3A: 12 + 8 + 6 = 26 books.
Class 3B: 30 + 15 + 20 = 65 books.
65 – 26 = 39 more books.

partialMarks.criterion: Reads the Class 3A bars using its scale and adds (26)
Reads the Class 3B bars using its scale and adds (65)
Subtracts to get 39

c.v: Mr Lim gives each pupil who chose Art or Music 3 coloured pencils. He has 80 coloured pencils. How many coloured pencils does he have left?
Art: 16 pupils. Music: 8 pupils. 16 + 8 = 24 pupils.
Pencils given out: 24 × 3 = 72.
80 – 72 = 8 coloured pencils left.

partialMarks.criterion: Reads the Art and Music bars and adds (24 pupils)
Multiplies by 3 to get 72 pencils
Subtracts from 80 to get 8
